account: The node's objective requires both extracting formal definitions from the Dung file and deriving design constraints for the many-to-many Q/A graph. These two tasks are analytically distinct and can be pursued in parallel: one child focuses on faithful source extraction with page markers, the other on the derivation of design constraints grounded in those definitions. The extraction child can be further decomposed to cover different definition families, and the derivation child can be structured to cover conflict/provenance and belief-revision separately. Each child is self-contained, uses the same frozen dossier, and does not depend on sibling outputs; the parent will synthesize the findings into a coherent node contribution.

children.objective: Extract from papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt, each anchored to the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) where it appears, the definitions of: (a) argumentation framework (set of arguments plus binary attack relation), (b) acceptability of an argument, (c) conflict-free set, and (d) admissible set. children.rationale: These four core definitions are the foundation for all subsequent semantics and design derivations. Isolating them into a dedicated extraction child ensures the source evidence is gathered precisely before any design inference is made.

children.objective: Derive, each explicitly labeled as design inference, how Dung's notions of argumentation framework, acceptability, conflict-free sets, and admissible sets can anchor answer-to-answer conflict and provenance relations in a many-to-many question/answer graph. Specifically, produce at least three design constraints: (1) how to model answers as arguments and conflicts as attack edges; (2) how to represent provenance relations (e.g., answer-addresses-question) as additional graph edges that do not alter conflict semantics; and (3) how admissible sets can define mutually consistent answer sets for a given question.
children.rationale: This child directly addresses D3 (answer-to-answer conflict/provenance relations) and D8 (contradiction behavior) by translating the formal definitions into design constraints for the graph substrate.

children.expected_contribution: A set of three or more design constraints for the belief-revision behavior of the substrate, specifying the semantics of acceptance and how revision is triggered, ready for synthesis.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: This derivation relies only on the definitions from the source file (in the dossier) and does not require sibling outputs.
children.objective: Derive, each explicitly labeled as design inference, how Dung's extension semantics (grounded, preferred, stable) can specify contradiction and belief-revision behavior in a many-to-many question/answer graph. Specifically, produce at least three design constraints: (1) how to use preferred extensions to define credulous acceptance of answers, allowing multiple competing answers to coexist; (2) how to use the grounded extension to define a skeptical set of answers that are accepted regardless of conflict; and (3) how belief revision can be modeled as updating the attack relation or the set of arguments and recomputing extensions.
children.rationale: This child directly addresses D8 (contradiction and belief-revision behavior) by translating the extension semantics into a design for how the system handles conflicting answers and updates its state.

decidability.account: The source file content is fully embedded in the dossier, so all extraction and derivation can be performed now. The acceptance conditions (at least four anchored findings, at least three design constraints) are clear, though some judgment is needed to decide what counts as a close paraphrase, so the acceptance is not fully mechanical.

synthesis_contract.acceptance_condition: The synthesized node contribution includes at least four source-anchored findings (with page markers) and at least three distinct design constraints for conflict/belief-revision semantics, all correctly labeled, satisfying the node's acceptance condition and contributing to demands D3, D8, D12, and D13.
synthesis_contract.conflict_policy: If a child's extraction conflicts with another (e.g., differing page markers or paraphrase interpretation), resolve by referring to the original text in the dossier; the most precise quote from the source takes precedence. Design constraints are independent and should not be merged unless they are complementary.
synthesis_contract.parent_question: Combine the source-anchored definitions from children 1 and 2 with the design derivations from children 3 and 4 to produce a coherent node contribution that: (a) presents at least four anchored findings on the Dung semantics, and (b) presents at least three design constraints for conflict/provenance and belief-revision, each clearly labeled as design inference. The synthesis must ensure that source claims are distinguished from design inferences and that all citations carry the exact page markers. It must also support the parent memo's demands D3, D8, D12, and D13.
